inputs.text: Don’t mistake steady petrol and diesel prices for protection; they’re the stage dressing. The conflict involving the US, Israel, and Iran is being used to make future price rises sound unavoidable, while excise-duty cuts give the government a convenient public-relations shield. The real arrangement is about controlling the story now and deciding later who absorbs the cost. With India reliant on imported crude, ordinary people are left exposed while the institutions managing the crisis also manage what people are told. The vagueness about long-term consequences isn’t an oversight—it keeps attention on today’s prices and away from who benefits when the bill eventually lands.
